descriptionChirho: Physical or general strength, force, or might inherent in a person, animal, or entity; the raw power exerted in action or possessed as an attribute, rendered consistently as Arabic quwwa, Korean him, and Swahili nguvu across all grammatical inflections and prepositional frames.

The capacity or ability to accomplish something, often referring to divine power or human capability to perform a task; distinguished from raw strength by Korean neungnyeok, Arabic al-qudra, Swahili uwezo/kadiri, and Spanish capacidad rather than the standard strength terms.

Material wealth, property, or economic resources; the substance or means available to a person, confirmed by Korean jaemul (wealth), Swahili utajiri (riches), and Hindi sampatti (property) diverging sharply from the standard strength translations.
